name: SQLite
description: Protects against destructive SQLite operations like DROP TABLE, \ DELETE without WHERE, and accidental data loss

destructive_patterns.name: stdin-unverified
destructive_patterns.description: sqlite3 receives indirect input that the engine cannot statically verify.
destructive_patterns.explanation: Materialize and review the exact SQL before piping or redirecting it into sqlite3.

destructive_patterns.name: drop-table
destructive_patterns.description: DROP TABLE permanently deletes the table (even with IF EXISTS). Verify it is intended.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
DROP TABLE permanently removes a table and all its data from the SQLite database. \ Unlike some other databases, SQLite has no recycle bin or undo mechanism. The IF \ EXISTS clause only prevents errors, it doesn't make the operation less destructive.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - .schema tablename: View table structure first \ - .dump tablename: Export table data as SQL backup \ - .backup: Create full database backup before dropping \ - ALTER TABLE ... RENAME: Rename instead of drop if reorganizing

destructive_patterns.name: delete-without-where
destructive_patterns.description: DELETE without WHERE deletes ALL rows. Add a WHERE clause.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
DELETE FROM without a WHERE clause removes every row from the table. This is \ almost always unintentional - if you truly want to remove all rows, TRUNCATE or \ DROP TABLE + CREATE is more explicit about the intent. SQLite doesn't support \ TRUNCATE, making this pattern especially dangerous.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - SELECT COUNT(*) FROM table: Check row count first \ - DELETE FROM table WHERE condition: Add explicit conditions \ - .backup before DELETE: Create backup first \ - Use transactions: BEGIN; DELETE ...; verify; COMMIT or ROLLBACK

destructive_patterns.name: vacuum-into
destructive_patterns.description: VACUUM INTO overwrites the target file if it exists.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
VACUUM INTO creates a new compacted copy of the database at the specified path. \ If a file already exists at that path, it will be overwritten without warning. \ This can accidentally destroy other databases or important files.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Check if target file exists before running \ - Use a unique filename with timestamp \ - .backup filename: Alternative backup method \ - Move existing file before VACUUM INTO

destructive_patterns.name: sqlite3-stdin
destructive_patterns.description: Running SQL from file could contain destructive commands. Review the file first.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Piping SQL from a file into sqlite3 executes all commands without review. The \ file may contain DROP TABLE, DELETE, or other destructive statements. If the \ file comes from an untrusted source or was auto-generated, it could cause \ unintended data loss.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Review the SQL file contents first \ - .backup before running: Create database backup \ - .read filename inside sqlite3: Allows Ctrl+C interruption \ - Run in a transaction: Wrap file contents in BEGIN/COMMIT
